content: Furniture AI: furnish the apartment you actually rent, from its real floor plan to one checked shopping list.
Ken Tam; solo final project.
Repository: NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE (URL; 'private repository' label if private). Online app: none (runs locally from a fresh clone; see README quick start).

One sentence: reads your building's published floor plan, lays out draft furniture in the rooms it finds, and fills each piece with a real, dated, sourced product within your budget, ending in a printable checklist and spreadsheet.
Small hero screenshot: NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE (clean plan canvas with furniture).

Who: a renter moving into an unfurnished apartment (the author's own move to The Archive, New Haven, is the worked example) who has a budget, a floor plan image from the building's website, and no tape measure.
How it's done today: screenshots of the plan, store tabs, guessing sizes, spreadsheets, and repeated trips back to check whether a sofa fits; secondhand sites add stale and unverifiable listings.
Cost: time and returns from wrong sizes. NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: sourced figures (e.g. moving/furnishing cost or return rates) with URLs; otherwise state the friction qualitatively without numbers.
Why it matters: a wrong-size purchase is expensive to return; a plan-aware, budget-honest list prevents it.

Named alternatives (descriptions to be checked by root against each product's own site, with access dates): IKEA Kreativ and room planners such as Planner 5D or RoomSketcher (drawing/visualisation tools), paid design services such as Havenly, and general chatbots such as ChatGPT.

Honest difference: starts from the building's own published plan, keeps kitchen/bath/closets clear, places pieces only in rooms whose use is confirmed by evidence, and ties every product to a dated page it actually read (price, size, condition, stock) under one hard budget. A chatbot can suggest furniture but doesn't read the plan into geometry, verify pages, or enforce a budget in code.
What it does NOT do: no 3D render, no purchases, no measured survey; fit is an estimate from printed sizes.
Comparison table: alternative | starts from your plan | real verified products | enforced budget | sources shown.

Diagram: browser -> FastAPI orchestrator (plain Python) -> four typed PydanticAI agents + one web-research call, all gpt-6-luna via the course Portkey Responses API; deterministic code for fetching, validation, placement, budget and the checklist; SQLite + content-addressed originals.

Plan Map agent (design_api.planmap_agent, prompt plan-map-v4-crops): input = one plan image plus two framed crops in ONE call; output = typed PlanMapOutput (room polygons, labels, printed sizes, walls, openings, fixtures). Tools: none (structured output only). Code validates geometry and decides each room's use (confirmed / uncertain / conflict).
Room Evidence agent (ai.room_agent, room-evidence-v5-geometry-shape): photos -> typed PhotoAnalysisOutput; photo geometry stays an unverified estimate. Tools: none. Used by the single-room flow.
Preference Edit agent (ai.pref_agent, preference-patch-v3): free text -> typed PreferencePatch applied by code. Tools: none.

Design Helper agent (design_api.assistant_agent, design-assistant-v1): answers questions and proposes typed changes; nothing changes until the user ticks and applies; never sees address, unit, images or links. Tools: none.

Web research call (research.py, furniture-products-v4-eligible-sites): Responses API with the built-in web_search tool only (<= 2 tool calls, low context, <= 1800 output tokens); results are leads filtered to approved stores/marketplaces and verified by reading each page.
Model choice: gpt-6-luna is the only model allowed on the course key; vision plus structured output plus built-in web search cover every need, so no second model.
Step-by-step real run on The Archive 1-bedroom plan, New only, $3,000 budget (NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: screenshots for each step and the ledger row ids).
Step 1: place created, building chosen from the checked list (no AI, no search).
Step 2: plan chosen; Read floor plan = one Plan Map call (NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: tokens). Show the AI map and the clean code-drawn plan, with rooms marked confirmed/uncertain.
Step 3: Arrange your space: deterministic arrangements; pieces only in usable rooms; anything without a valid spot goes to Not placed.

Step 4: Choose furniture: Find furniture = one web-research call per piece type (NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: number of calls and pages checked), then page checks two at a time; only options that fit and are within the piece's share and the whole budget are recommended.
Step 5: Choose for me / manual choices; the server refuses anything over the remaining item budget.
Step 6: Final checklist and both downloads (printable HTML and Excel) (NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: screenshots).
What each agent did vs what code did, in one table for this run.

Table from the usage ledger for the real run: per call kind (plan_map, web_research furniture, design_assistant if used): input tokens, cached input tokens, output tokens, web_search_calls, estimated cost. NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: all numbers.
Typical run cost = sum of the run's ledger rows (NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE). Rate table and search fee from usage.py (state its date and that costs are estimates from returned usage, not invoices).
Per user per month: NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: stated assumption (e.g. runs per user per month) times measured run cost; scale to 100 and 10,000 users, showing the formula.

Cost controls actually built: saved plan maps reused by input hash + prompt version; identical searches share one in-flight request and a 10-minute cache; pieces of the same type and size share one search; the new-item search is skipped when 3+ saved options already fit the budget; no automatic second search (Search more is explicit); refusing marketplaces are skipped without spending a search; session $2.00, daily $3.00 and 12-requests-per-10-minutes limits, reserved atomically before each call.

Quality tradeoff evidence: offline simulated benchmark (docs/evidence/offline_search_benchmark.md: 0.594 s serial vs 0.372 s with two parallel checks, identical decisions; SIMULATED, not live). Live tradeoff: fewer checks per search can miss supply; NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: any live comparison, or state that none was measured.

Attacks: prompt injection in web pages, listings and photo text (treated as untrusted evidence, never instructions; listings are parsed deterministically and never sent to the model); SSRF through user or search URLs (SafeFetcher: public IPs only, DNS pinning, every redirect hop checked, size/type caps); unknown or private sellers (hard allowlist: Amazon, Article, IKEA, Target for new; AptDeco, Chairish, eBay, Facebook Marketplace items, Craigslist posts for used).

Malfunction: invented geometry or facts (typed outputs validated by code; missing facts stay unknown; unreadable plans get no automatic placement; bath fixtures in a 'bedroom' = conflict, no bed); wrong actions (helper proposals need explicit apply; versions are append-only with optimistic concurrency); loops (one call per request, bounded retries, bounded page checks).

Overspending (money): the server refuses any product over the remaining item budget (exact figures in the message); over-budget earlier choices are flagged, never silently deleted. Overspending (tokens): atomic reservations against session/daily/rate limits; a cap pauses with a plain message.
Show at least one defense working (NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE: screenshot and/or test output). Candidate tests (offline, deterministic):
backend/tests/test_domain.py::test_injected_instruction_cannot_change_budget_or_policy
backend/tests/test_api.py::test_listing_import_injection_condition_and_raw_source

backend/tests/test_env_and_fetch.py::test_private_and_unsafe_urls_blocked, ::test_dns_to_private_blocked, ::test_redirect_to_metadata_blocked, ::test_redirect_to_host_rebinding_to_private_blocked, ::test_public_status_never_contains_key
backend/tests/test_source_boundary.py::test_unknown_sites_are_refused_without_any_network_access, ::test_a_store_redirect_to_an_unknown_site_is_never_contacted
backend/tests/test_resale_trust.py::test_a_redirect_to_an_unapproved_site_is_refused_before_connecting

backend/tests/test_budget_selection.py::test_a_14500_sofa_on_a_3000_budget_is_never_recommended_selectable_or_accepted, ::test_earlier_over_budget_choices_are_kept_flagged_searchable_and_repairable_one_at_a_time
backend/tests/test_limits_and_speed.py::test_reserved_and_settled_costs_count_and_the_boundary_is_atomic, ::test_concurrent_identical_searches_share_one_ai_request_and_the_cache_expires
backend/tests/test_domain.py::test_ledger_limits_and_concurrency; backend/tests/test_find_furniture.py::test_rate_limit_pauses_the_group_with_a_clear_message
backend/tests/test_design_assistant.py::test_the_model_sees_the_design_but_not_the_address_unit_or_sources, ::test_proposed_changes_apply_exactly_once_after_review
backend/tests/test_supply_and_review.py::test_when_every_selected_marketplace_refuses_nothing_is_searched_or_checked
Source provenance: originals immutable and content-addressed; every derivative has parent id, hash, method/model/prompt version and timestamp; checklist rows link only to approved sources.

Real user: NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE (the pilot the root is asking the user to run now: who, task, time taken with the app vs the usual way, quote, screenshot). If no pilot happens, say so plainly; no outside pilot is claimed.
The author's own run: NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE (time from plan to checklist; items found within $3,000; pieces left missing and why).
Sourced context numbers: NEED_ROOT_EVIDENCE (each with a URL and access date).
Evidence labels: real run / offline test / estimate, kept separate.

Limits: the plan map is an AI reading of a picture, not a survey; fit is approximate; marketing/3D plans may be unreadable (then no automatic placement). Secondhand supply is thin: eBay answers HTTP 403, AptDeco often shows robot checks, Chairish is readable but often above budget; the app never bypasses them. The checked catalog is small (IKEA, Article, one Amazon item) and prices/stock may change. Local only, no hosting; no purchases.

Next month: more store adapters and sizes; a measured fit check with the user's own wall lengths; a hosted version with accounts; a real multi-user pilot with timing; better plan reading for 3D renders.
